Pawse is running on the VM, and all its pages load over Tailscale.

**Open these in your browser:**
- Main app (the Mimi demo plays on the first screen, no keys needed): http://100.120.75.21:8765/
- React voice-first app: http://100.120.75.21:8765/app/
- API docs: http://100.120.75.21:8765/docs

From the VM I checked that `/`, `/app/`, `/docs` and `/api/v1/demo/mimi` all return 200. I didn't click through the demo in a real browser.

⚠️ **The microphone won't work at the URLs above.** Browsers only allow mic access on `https` or on `localhost`, and these are plain `http` on an IP address. If you want to try the voice features, open an SSH tunnel from PowerShell:
```
ssh -L 8765:127.0.0.1:8765 azureuser@100.120.75.21
```
Then go to http://localhost:8765/app/ instead.

To get it running I:
- created `.venv` and installed `requirements-dev.txt`
- ran `npm install` and `npm run build` in `web/`, so the React app is served at `/app/`
- started uvicorn on port 8765 with `PAWSE_ALLOWED_HOSTS=100.120.75.21`. The app's host allowlist was rejecting the Tailscale IP with "Invalid host header". I set it only for this process and didn't change `.env`.

The server is PID 3030952, and its log is at `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-azureuser-pawse/6cd3ea3d-648c-415e-8e3e-8ec19c9e6d60/scratchpad/uvicorn.log`. It keeps running after this session ends. I can stop it whenever you want.

**https://ari-personal-development.tail512e9e.ts.net/app/**

Your browser will ask for camera and microphone permission the first time; click Allow. Any device logged into your Tailscale network can open this link, including your phone.

`/`, `/app/` and `/api/v1/demo/mimi` all return 200 over HTTPS. I haven't opened the camera myself, since that needs a real browser on your side.

What I changed:
- Ran `sudo tailscale serve --bg 8765`, which forwards `https://…ts.net` to the app on port 8765. This setting stays on after a VM reboot; turn it off with `sudo tailscale serve --https=443 off`.
- Restarted the server (now PID 3042013) with the HTTPS hostname added to `PAWSE_ALLOWED_HOSTS`. That's set for this process only, not in `.env`.
